<SUMMARY>Global geopolitical and economic landscapes are dominated by escalating competition in critical technologies and resources. The United States imposed export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models for foreign nationals, raising concerns about a potential global AI arms race and prompting calls for AI sovereignty. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) reported significant revenue growth driven by AI demand, while China's export curbs on tungsten threaten Japan's AI chip supply chain. Critical mineral supply chain resilience remains a key focus, with the US government initiating efforts to diversify sources away from China and acquiring stakes in domestic mining operations. The ongoing conflict in Iran continues to impact global oil prices and economic growth, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining a critical choke point, despite President Trump's announcement of a potential peace deal and reopening.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>US export controls on Anthropic models Fable 5 and Mythos 5 could trigger a global AI arms race, prompting nations to accelerate their own AI advancements and policies. China's export curbs on tungsten threaten Japan’s AI chip supply chain, indicating a vulnerability in critical material access. The UAE's oil giant states that full Strait of Hormuz flows will not resume until the first half of 2027, despite President Trump's assertion of an imminent reopening, posing continued energy trade restrictions.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) posted strong May sales, with revenue surging 30% due to AI demand. TSM's profit margin stands at 47.34% and net income at $55.13 billion (FY25), making it a top pick for analysts, with a 9.80% upside. Pingtung broke ground on Taiwan's first semiconductor supply chain park. China implemented export curbs on tungsten, which threatens Japan’s AI chip supply chain.

**Africa:**
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) imposed a cobalt export ban, which could trouble global EV battery supply chains. The race for East Africa’s critical minerals is upending regional conservation efforts. The US government met with 54 nations in Washington to build a mineral economy without China, connecting efforts back to US soil. The US government also took a 10% stake in a mining company to secure critical minerals, as 16 minerals are not produced in America.

**Europe:**
President Donald Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron will meet over dinner at the Palace of Versailles after the G7 summit in France. President Trump will also speak with several European leaders, many of whom he has argued with over trade, tariffs, Ukraine, and NATO. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Ireland's leader and the French President ahead of the G7 summit, advocating for middle powers to unite rather than compete for American favor. Rising energy bills worldwide, driven by significant restrictions on energy trade through the Strait of Hormuz, are fueling a global home battery boom. The UK set out an AI infrastructure push at London Tech Week. France’s Électronique 2030 program committed over €5 billion to revitalize its semiconductor industry, designed to catalyze €16 billion in total investment. Orderly listed an SK Hynix token for trading with 10x leverage, democratizing access to high-demand tech stocks.

**Americas:**
Amazon.com, Inc. completed the sale of C$14 billion ($10 billion) in investment-grade bonds in Canada to finance a $200 billion AI data center investment spree. Applied Digital Corporation, a Dallas-based designer and operator of AI data centers, was named "Best Data Center in the Americas 2025." The data center boom is colliding with competitive House districts in the midterms. The US government ordered Anthropic to pull Claude Fable and Mythos AI models, citing national security concerns and a widespread vulnerability, to which Anthropic complied by suspending access for all foreign nationals globally. Tech experts advocate for Sovereign AI amid these US actions, warning of business risks from service suspensions. Bechtel will build a $100 billion semiconductor plant, the biggest in the US. Forge Nano secured a semiconductor wafer fab equipment order from a leading photonics technology company for commercial integrated photonics manufacturing. Jamaica is planning to drill for oil, following successful exploration in Guyana. A master of a ghost fleet tanker, Avtandil Kalandadze, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court for refusing to obey orders from the US Coast Guard during a pursuit, after historically transporting Iran- and Venezuela-origin oil. The US, Greece, Cyprus, and Israel launched an East Med Energy Center in Houston.

**Oceania:**
A new report found that Australia has valuable cards to play in the AI future. Sharon AI, an Australian neocloud company, announced a six-year strategic compute collaboration with Nvidia (NVDA) to enable 72 megawatts of new data centers. Sharon AI stock surged 25% following this deal.
</EXEC>

<MILITARY>
**Americas:**
President Donald Trump stated that a US military strike killed the leader of the Tren de Aragua gang with help from Venezuela, showcasing an unclassified video of a building exploding.

**West Asia:**
Families of Indian sailors killed in a US military attack in the Strait of Hormuz are demanding accountability for commercial vessel attacks. Missile defense systems worked against Iran, but may not be effective against China.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
**Americas:**
SpaceX's massive $2 trillion IPO has challenged the 'Magnificent Seven' moniker, as its valuation now surpasses Tesla and Meta, impacting market strategies for tech-stock labeling.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Indian companies like Ultratech Cement and Vedanta are rapidly investing in electric trucks, driven by fluctuating diesel prices and a focus on sustainability. India's diversified equity market offers stability and broad exposure, contrasting with concentrated risks in other global markets. An FIR was registered in Mumbai against eight government staff for failing to turn up for Booth Level Officer duty. An excise raid in Bhubaneswar’s Salia Sahi slum busted an illegal liquor distillery, seizing 5,000 litres and destroying 12,200 litres of wash, with three arrests. Eight people were injured in Koyilandy, Kozhikode, after two cars collided head-on. Mala Roy resigned from the Trinamool Congress and as women’s wing chief, with Alifa Ahmed appointed as the new president, reflecting turmoil in TMC’s south Kolkata base. Tech experts and public commentary suggest India needs AI sovereignty and supply-chain resilience in the wake of US restrictions on Anthropic models.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
President Donald Trump will meet with US partners in the Middle East at the G7 summit in France, underscoring the outsized role of the war in Iran. President Trump announced an Iran peace deal for Sunday, promising the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a claim later contradicted by Iran which still differs over key points including waterway management and payments. The UAE’s oil giant stated that full Hormuz flows will not resume until the first half of 2027. The World Bank lowered its global growth forecast for the remainder of 2026, attributing it to Trump's Iran war driving up energy prices, inflation, and debt costs. The conflict in Iran has contributed to soaring U.S. oil profits and stock gains. A secret Qatari protection deal was presented to Iran prior to the war with the US and Israel. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman canceled an Abu Dhabi trip amid tensions, potentially hindering OpenAI's Middle East expansion and affecting global AI infrastructure and investment dynamics. AI was used to create a film showing violence in Iran, raising concerns about AI and the war. Israel Innovation Authority and Israeli DDR&D (MAFAT) launched a NIS 150 million initiative to advance Israel’s next generation of photonic chips.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming period will likely see continued intensification of technology competition, particularly in AI and semiconductors, exacerbated by export controls and national security directives. The push for critical mineral supply chain diversification will remain a high priority for Western nations. The ongoing conflict in Iran and its global energy implications will continue to be a dominant factor shaping economic stability and international relations, with the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz remaining paramount.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
